author: Mark Atwood
text:
Workspace-architectural decision required before this sweep can be worked: pick among three mitigations for the per-type READONLY/UPDATE_ALLOWED string list pattern:

(1) Move readonly + update-allowed lists to a marker-trait method on each JmapObject. Compiler enforces every type names its server-set fields once. Handler reads from the trait. No new crates needed. Aligns with the workspace's hand-written-trait posture.

(2) Derive the lists from a struct-level attribute via a proc-macro that lives in the types crate. Introduces a proc-macro dep which the workspace currently avoids.

(3) Tag fields with #[serde(skip_deserializing)] on a *patch* type (separate from the get type). Requires every type's patch-shape to be wholly separate from its get-shape — a structural commitment the workspace has not made.

Recommendation: Path (1). Aligns with existing posture (hand-written traits everywhere; no proc-macros), doesn't introduce new crates, doesn't require structural separation of patch/get types. The trait method on JmapObject would be something like:

    fn readonly_fields() -> &'static [&'static str];
    fn writable_update_fields() -> &'static [&'static str];

with a default impl returning empty slices (so unmigrated types remain wide-open until migrated). Handlers grep would change from CONTACT_READONLY.iter() to O::readonly_fields().iter().

Cross-extension implications: All 8 types crates (jmap-mail-types, jmap-chat-types, jmap-calendars-types, etc.) need every JmapObject impl to add the two methods. Mechanical change, ~30 lines per impl. Once landed, the *_READONLY consts and *_UPDATE_ALLOWED consts in all 8 server crates collapse to direct trait calls. Maintenance invariant becomes compiler-enforced.

Filed as human because the workspace has multiple plausible mitigations with non-trivial structural commitments. The decision is not the agent's call.
